pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Severe neuro-visceral pain out of proportion to exam combined with urine that darkens to a port-wine hue upon UV/sunlight exposure, provoked by fasting and aggravated by a cytochrome P450-inducing antiemetic (metoclopramide). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Caused by an autosomal dominant deficiency in porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD), the third enzyme in the heme synthesis pathway. Extreme caloric restriction and porphyrinogenic xenobiotics (like metoclopramide) induce hepatic ALA synthase 1 (ALAS1). This results in a catastrophic accumulation of neurotoxic intermediates—delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). These neurotoxins trigger autonomic hyperactivity (tachycardia, hypertension), hypothalamic dysfunction causing SIADH (hyponatremia), central neuropsychiatric disturbances, and a severe motor-predominant axonal neuropathy mimicking Guillain-Barré syndrome. Oxidation of colorless PBG to porphobilin upon light exposure creates the classic dark red/brown urine.
